problems: Header 'Join the install list' button fails contrast (2.32:1, dark ink on blue) at every width above 760px because '.nav a' overrides the button text colour; axe flags it at 1440
Maintainability: CSS and script compressed into one-line rules, SVG colours hard-coded in JS and markup instead of tokens, a no-op opacity 'transition', innerHTML used with localStorage data
Keyboard/AT gaps: no skip link, Escape does not close the mobile menu, form errors not associated with their fields (no aria-invalid or aria-describedby)

reason: B works better on the phone (real menu with 48px links, a chart that redraws for 324px with no sideways swiping, no overflow even with extreme input) and handles the storage-failure path honestly. Its main defect, the low-contrast header CTA, is a one-line CSS fix. A has cleaner code and a richer artifact, but mobile needs real work: no menu, a 700px swipe strip and 21px targets. If A had a recomposed mobile strip and a menu, I would ship A for its code quality and its stronger keyboard and error handling.
